clue.text: Painting Orson embraced by Liz, destined for strawberry leaf

parts.note: painting is an art

indicators.note: being embraced means held in someone's arms, so one name sits inside the other

parts.note: Liz Hurley, the actress and model
Orson Welles, the film director

explanation.surface: A portrait of Orson Welles being hugged by Liz Hurley, bound for some leafy honour.
explanation.walkthrough: The strawberry leaf is the emblem on a duke's coronet; Arthur Wellesley became Duke of Wellington.
explanation.definitionFit: Wellesley was later ennobled as a duke, whose coronet bears strawberry leaves, so he was bound for a dukedom.

clue.text: Sergeant wanted to do it to faces missing the 8 thing

definitions.text: to do it to faces missing the 8 thing

indicators.note: a wanted man is on the run, a loose word suggesting the letters of the rank are let loose too

parts.note: the eight letters of the rank, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: An army sergeant longing to do something to the faces of people who lack a certain splendid thing.
explanation.walkthrough: Francis Thompson's poem has 'your estranged faces, That miss the many-splendoured thing' (8-down); the definition quotes it.
explanation.definitionFit: In Thompson's poem the faces that miss the many-splendoured thing are estranged, so that is what was done to them.

clue.text: … patriots at heart

indicators.note: the heart of a word is its central part, so only its middle letters are kept

parts.note: the four central letters of the eight-letter word

explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis stands in for the definition, carrying on from the clue before: the setter leaves the solver to see a group of three.
explanation.definitionFit: The answer is a set of three, a group the ellipsis leaves the solver to supply from the letters found.

clue.text: My first, says my second, is an 8 thing: nothing goes cheaply

definitions.text: My first, says my second, is an 8 thing

parts.note: love is zero in tennis
something that goes cheaply goes for a song

explanation.surface: A riddle about a thing with many splendours, where nothing sells for much.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a riddle: the song 'Love Is a Many-Splendoured Thing' says its first word is a many-splendoured thing, so it is a song about love.
explanation.definitionFit: A song titled 'Love Is a Many-Splendoured Thing' is a romantic ballad, the classic example of the genre.

clue.text: Alternative to tram without the groove, producing the unkindest cut

indicators.note: used in its old sense of outside, so one word stands around the other

parts.note: another form of public transport
a rut is a worn groove

explanation.surface: A tram that has lost its groove gives way to another vehicle, a harsh blow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' looks like 'lacking', but it means outside. In Julius Caesar, Brutus's stab is 'the most unkindest cut of all'.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's Mark Antony calls the stabbing by Caesar's friend Brutus the most unkindest cut of all.

clue.text: Released before autumn, "The Descent of Icarus"

parts.note: set free
the American word for autumn

explanation.surface: A painting called The Descent of Icarus, released ahead of the autumn season.
explanation.definitionFit: Icarus plummeted from the sky without any means of slowing down, an unchecked plunge through the air.

clue.text: Student distorts rising proliferation of housing

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising means the letters are read from bottom to top

parts.note: L for learner, as on a learner driver's plate
bends out of shape

explanation.surface: A student skews a report about the rising spread of new housing.
explanation.definitionFit: Urban sprawl is the uncontrolled spread of buildings across countryside on the edge of towns.

clue.text: Iridescent mother of American city was effusive about loan (there's a thing!)

indicators.note: one word goes around the other, enclosing it

parts.note: informal for mother
the city's abbreviation in the possessive: 'of New York' becomes New York's
poured out words
a loan is something you lend

explanation.surface: An American city's mother gushed about a loan, with an exclamation at the end.
explanation.walkthrough: '(there's a thing!)' nods to the song 'Love Is a Many-Splendoured Thing'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something iridescent shows shimmering changing colours, so it seems to have many splendours.

clue.text: Engineers come back inside to have another look at the tank

indicators.note: one piece sits within the other

parts.note: French for to see again, as in au revoir

indicators.note: coming back means going the other way, so the letters are read backwards

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers; plural REs

explanation.surface: Engineers return to inspect a tank once more.
explanation.walkthrough: The French verb revoir (to see again) is the container; REs, the Royal Engineers, go in backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A reservoir is a large tank or basin used for storing water.

clue.text: See 11
Rejuvenation requires hard gold cash, retaining dividers: Bond must take the blame

indicators.note: to retain is to hold within, so one word keeps others inside it

parts.note: H for hard, as on pencils
gold in heraldry
money is cash; it holds the rest
the setter's link for the remaining letters; no standard sense of dividers gives them
cement bonds things together
take the rap: THE RAP is the blame

explanation.surface: Getting young again means hard cash, and Bond must carry the can.
explanation.walkthrough: The cash word wraps round the rest, its last letter ending the whole phrase. 'Dividers' has no standard sense giving its letters; it may be setter's whimsy. To take the rap is to take the blame.
explanation.definitionFit: This treatment replaces declining sex hormones, and is promoted as restoring youthful vigour, hence rejuvenation.

clue.text: See 11
The little g____er

parts.note: surface: a gap-fill puzzle about some small creature or person
setter's reading: the gap holds the smallest pig of a litter, and filling it makes a word for a pig

explanation.walkthrough: Filling the blanks gives GRUNTER, a pig, and the smallest one in a litter is the word in the gap.
explanation.definitionFit: The weakest, smallest piglet of a litter is called by this name, so it is the little grunter.

clue.text: Fish comes second to beer and tripe

parts.note: a fish
abbreviation for second
wallop is British slang for beer

explanation.surface: A pub meal: fish served after the beer, with tripe on the side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tripe' looks like more food on the menu; it means nonsense.
explanation.definitionFit: Tripe in the sense of rubbish talk is a synonym of this British word for nonsense.

clue.text: When the Levellers did their stuff?

definitions.text: When the Levellers did their stuff?

parts.words: When the Levellers did their stuff?
parts.note: surface: asking at what period the 17th-century radical group was active
setter's reading: people who level things make them even, and that process is what they were doing

explanation.walkthrough: The Levellers were a radical English Civil War movement; the question mark flags a pun on making things level.
explanation.definitionFit: Read as a word for making smooth, the answer is the levellers' activity; read normally it is a time of day.

clue.text: Is 4's first subject atomically identical?

parts.note: taken as written
the first word of 4-down means nothing, which is O
a subject of discussion

explanation.surface: A question asking whether some subject is identical at the atomic level.
explanation.walkthrough: 4-down's first word is LOVE, nothing, which is the letter O.
explanation.definitionFit: Isotopes are atoms of one element with the same atomic number but differing mass, so chemically alike.

clue.text: Muddy mark for childless masons?

parts.note: sine prole, Latin for without issue, as abbreviated in genealogies
Freemasons meet in a lodge

explanation.surface: A dirty smudge left by Freemasons who have no children.
explanation.walkthrough: s.p. (sine prole) marks someone who died childless in family trees.
explanation.definitionFit: A splodge is a messy blot or smear, such as one left by mud.

clue.text: Reproduce the state of the poor emu's tail

indicators.note: something in poor condition is in a bad way, so its letters are in disorder

parts.note: the eight letters of the phrase

explanation.surface: Copy the bedraggled condition of a sorry emu's tail feathers.
explanation.definitionFit: To simulate is to imitate or recreate something, a synonym of copying or reproducing it.

clue.text: No boarder keeps names of subject of air on the pipes

definitions.text: subject of air on the pipes

indicators.note: to keep something is to hold it inside

parts.note: a pupil who goes home each night rather than boarding at school
N for name, doubled for the plural

explanation.surface: A boy who does not board at school keeps the names of a tune played on bagpipes.
explanation.walkthrough: The Irish ballad, sung to the Londonderry Air, opens 'the pipes, the pipes are calling'.
explanation.definitionFit: The ballad is addressed to a young man named in its title, so he is the subject of the air.

clue.text: Not enough hours to transport milk to cafe

indicators.note: transporting something carries it off, so these letters are moved into a new arrangement

parts.note: the ten letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A dairy worker complains there are too few hours to deliver milk to the cafe.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacking time means the available hours fall short of what is needed, a direct paraphrase.

clue.text: See 11
Ditch partially enclosed during raising of 11 10 20 12

indicators.note: something that happens during another thing falls within it
in a down clue, raising means the letters run upwards

parts.note: the usual initials of the long answer in those lights

indicators.note: only part of the word is used, its opening letters

parts.note: the first three letters, also the business abbreviation

explanation.surface: A ditch partly closed off while the treatment is being given a boost.
explanation.walkthrough: Hormone replacement therapy is normally called HRT; ENC is the abbreviation for enclosed on letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A trench is a long narrow ditch dug in the ground.

clue.text: Take food from the right girl

indicators.note: reading from the right means going right to left, backwards

parts.note: to dine is to eat

explanation.surface: Take food away from the girl on the right.
explanation.definitionFit: Enid is a girl's given name, and crosswords freely define first names this way.

clue.text: Solver's double soon holds setter, a priest, to the means of entering Oxford University

indicators.note: to hold something is to have it inside

parts.note: taken as written; it holds the next piece
the setter refers to themself as me
Eli, the priest in the Book of Samuel
a key lets you in
abbreviation

explanation.surface: A setter and a priest seeking a way into Oxford University, with a double soon on hand.
explanation.walkthrough: The solver is 'you', so the solver's double is a person resembling you. Eli is the priest who raised Samuel.
explanation.definitionFit: A double of the solver resembles the solver, who is addressed as you, so is a person similar to you.

clue.text: See 23
Ex-Chancellor was burnt, they tell me

indicators.note: something told is spoken, so this is how a word sounds

parts.note: coal is the fuel that was burnt

explanation.surface: A former Chancellor was burnt, or so people say.
explanation.walkthrough: Helmut Kohl was Chancellor of Germany; the surface suggests a British Chancellor of the Exchequer.
explanation.definitionFit: Helmut Kohl led Germany as its head of government from 1982 to 1998.

clue.text: In endless night across the water it makes one yawn

indicators.note: without an end, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: French for in
French for night

explanation.surface: Something that makes you yawn during a sleepless night overseas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Across the water' tells you both words are French, from across the Channel.
explanation.definitionFit: Ennui is listless boredom, and boredom is what makes people yawn.

clue.text: Sheriff's officer's not to miss the post

parts.note: to catch is not to miss
a pole is a post

explanation.surface: A sheriff's deputy is not to miss the mail.
explanation.walkthrough: A catchpole was a historical bailiff who arrested debtors.
explanation.definitionFit: A catchpole was a medieval officer of the law, a bailiff who made arrests for debt, serving the sheriff.
